pairs.difference: A: the beach ball is one clean circle with panels that read as thin seams. It is a true sphere, and its off-range numbers come from the shape being a circle, not from bad form. B: the tumbleweed's twigs are drawn as uniform fat rods with rounded cut ends, all the same thickness. The ball reads as a tidy round bundle, and the edge has blobby stick ends poking out.
pairs.fix: Draw the tumbleweed as a loose, airy tangle of very thin, wiry, brittle twigs that taper to fine points. Make it slightly lopsided, with lots of gaps where the background shows through. No thick rods or rounded stick ends.

pairs.difference: A: the book has straight cover edges, tight corners, flat bookmark ribbons and a crisp page block. B: the belt strap is a thick, even rubbery band coiled into a perfect spiral. The buckle is an oversized round puck with a pillowy rim, and the silhouette is all soft curves with no tight corners. The buckle is about as big as the whole coil.
pairs.fix: Draw a thin, flat leather belt with sharp straight edges. Coil it loosely and let it overlap unevenly. Give it a smaller rectangular metal buckle with a thin frame and a prong, about a third of the coil's width.

pairs.difference: A: the boots have short, stubby shafts and fat rounded toes. The pull-tabs are thick loops, and the spurs are oversized star rowels on chunky straps. The heel and shaft corners are soft blobs. B: the sneakers have a believable sole and toe-box proportion, and the laces are thin.
pairs.fix: Draw taller, slimmer cowboy boots with a pointed toe, a sharp stacked heel with a crisp corner, and narrow pull-tabs. Make the spurs small, with a thin strap and a small rowel.

pairs.difference: A: the glass has straight tapered walls and a thin straw and umbrella stick, matching the reference card. B: the neon ice-cream sign is a flat panel with a scalloped scoop and a straight-sided cone. Its contour is plausible for a sign, so the shape gives no clear tell.

A: the viewer has a flat-faced head with crisp bevels, a thin side handle and a straight post, all in believable proportion. B: the logs are short, fat cylinders, and the ring stones are swollen pillow lumps. The coffee pot is squat with a thick handle, and the flames are smooth blobs. Every part is inflated to the same toy-like chunkiness.
pairs.fix: Draw longer, thinner split logs with rough flat cut ends. Use irregular, flatter stones with some sharp edges, and give the enamel coffee pot a thin wire handle and a slender spout.

pairs.difference: A: the cowboy hat's crown is a swollen rounded dome, and the brim is a thick, soft cushion curling up at both sides with a blobby outline and no crisp edge. The hatband is a fat tube. B: the mortarboard is a flat square board with straight runs and tight corners, and the tassel cord is thin.
pairs.fix: Draw the hat with a thin, flat felt brim that has a crisp edge, and a creased crown with a sharp pinched front and a center dent. Make the hatband a thin flat ribbon.

pairs.difference: B: the lighthouse matches the reference card. A: the windmill's wooden tower legs and cross-braces are chunky beams, and the base is a soft stepped block. The tail vane is a thick small paddle on a short stubby boom, and the wheel looks heavy relative to the thin tower a real windmill has.
pairs.fix: Draw the windmill tower as a tall, slender lattice of thin metal or wood struts. Use a long thin tail boom with a flat vane, and a wheel of many thin blades on a light rim.

pairs.difference: A: the cactus trunk and arms are smooth, fat sausage tubes with round ends and even thickness, with blobby flower petals on top. The arms are short and the trunk is wide, like a plush toy. B: the topiary spiral tiers have a leafy, irregular edge and believable stacked proportions.
pairs.fix: Draw a tall saguaro with a slender trunk and narrower arms that bend at a clear elbow. Add crisp vertical ribs and a fine spiny edge, and a small flower on top.

pairs.difference: A: the saddle's horn is a short knob and the cantle is a swollen rounded hump. The fender is a thick slab, and the stirrups are fat rounded loops with chunky plates. The proportions are short and compact for a saddle. B: the boxing gloves read as correctly swollen padded forms, with a thumb and cuff in the right relation.
pairs.fix: Draw a longer, lower western saddle with a thin, tall horn and a flatter seat. Use thin leather fenders and narrow wooden stirrups with straight sides.

pairs.difference: A: the suitcase matches the reference card, with a flat box, a corner guard and a handle loop. B: the mower has a thin tubular handle bar, wheels in proportion and a deck that is rounded but plausible. Neither silhouette shows inflation or missing parts.

A: the oil lamp has a slim glass chimney, a thin ring handle and a crisp stepped foot. B: the lantern's cage wires are thick sausage bars, the top bail handle is a fat loop and the base is a swollen puck. The corners are soft everywhere, and the frame is stubby and toy-like.
pairs.fix: Draw the lantern with a thin wire bail handle and a slim wire guard cage. Give it a narrow tin base with a crisp stepped rim and a taller glass globe.

pairs.difference: A: the wagon wheel's iron tire and felloe form a very thick, rounded rim. The spokes are fat even pegs and the hub is a big blob, so the wheel reads like a toy. B: the submarine is a plausibly rounded hull with a thin periscope and small fins.
pairs.fix: Draw a wagon wheel with a narrow flat iron tire and a thin wooden rim. Use slender tapered spokes and a modest hub with a crisp flat face.

pattern: Generated cards inflate everything to the same toy chunkiness. Thin parts like stirrups, spokes, wire handles, tower struts, twigs and hatbands become even sausages. Flat planes like hat brims, saddle skirts and belt straps swell into soft cushions. Corners round off into blobs, and the objects come out shorter and stubbier than real ones. Real cards keep tight bevels and slender parts where the real object has them.
